Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15 10:00 PT
Duration: 68 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Priya, Diego, Linh, Marcus, Zoe, Samir + rotating engs

[00:00] Priya: ok, hey team thanks for jumping on, short scrum. We saw the nightly eval spike — a quality dip — on the inference v2.3 canary, so want a quick scrub and decide release gate.
[00:17] Diego: yeah the alerts came in at 03:12 UTC, automated evals, about 0.8% overall rouge increase but concentrated on instructions, like persona prompts. Not huge but consistent.
[00:35] Linh: i pulled the evals earlier — it's not tokenization, seems generator-level hallucinations on a handful of prompts, likely related to the last kernel patch or the quantize path. Could be KV cache invalidation too, but less likely.
[00:48] Marcus: timeline wise we planned to ship 2.3 tomorrow morning, so we need a gate decision soon. Do we block, ship with monitor, or rollback?
[01:02] Zoe: QA saw the same in our small manual smoke, reproduced on dedicated with fp16-quantize flow. Not exclusive to one GPU type but more frequent on older drivers.
[01:18] Samir: also saw elevated tail latency on the canary at the same time window, might be correlated — when kv cache thrash happens we sometimes see decode loops, but ambiguous.
[01:32] Diego: hypothesis A: kernel change introduced slight divergence in attention normalization; hypothesis B: quantize config changed rounding behavior. We'll bisect.
[01:50] Priya: ok prioritize hypotheses — Diego you take kernel bisect, Linh you build a minimal reproducible eval, Zoe you automate the smoke, Samir you limit traffic. Marcus you own gate. Agreed?
[02:05] Group: yes / yep / agreed.
[02:20] Diego: quick note — the bisect might take a few iterations, especially if it's multi-factor (kernel + qconfig). I'll start with the last three kernel commits and swap them on canary.
[02:40] Linh: i'll port the failing prompt set into the eval harness and add golden outputs. Need to confirm metrics: we care about instruction-following F1, hallucination rate, and a composite quality score.
[02:58] Marcus: define pass/fail thresholds now: if composite quality delta > 0.4% on canary relative to baseline, block. If delta between 0.2-0.4% hold and require PM sign-off + extra regression test.
[03:18] Zoe: note that our earlier threshold was too permissive — small changes ripple; i'm going to tighten checks for the smoke run.
[03:34] Priya: customer comms — we might need a short note if customer-facing anomalies observed. We'll prepare a draft but hold until root cause is clearer.
[03:48] Diego: one more ops mitigation: Samir can we add a temporary routing rule to divert 30% of production traffic away from the affected model variant to the older 2.2 pool?
[04:05] Samir: yes i can add a traffic split and rate cap; i'll do 30% as a safe number and monitor error budgets. Will push rule by EOD.
[04:20] Linh: i want to run model-level logits diffs to see where the divergence starts — prefix length seems to matter.
[04:32] Priya: that's important for reproducer. Also list of customers who saw anomalies? Marcus any telemetry?
[04:45] Marcus: small set of customers hit anomalous outputs — sandbox tenants and two early enterprise pilots. I'll add them to the comms list.
[05:00] Zoe: what about a hotfix we can ship fast? If it's qconfig we could flip a conservative quant path back. That could be lower risk than rolling entire kernel.
[05:14] Diego: maybe, but hotfix risk is we introduce perf regression; need to run perf bench. We'll schedule quick perf runs in parallel.
[05:28] Priya: decision framework: if bisect finds culprit in kernel and urgent patch is nontrivial -> rollback. If qconfig toggle fixes and perf hit is small -> hotfix toggle + targeted rollout. If ambiguous -> hold release.
[05:46] Samir: i'll prepare rollback runbook and smoke the rollback path in staging to ensure we can flip quickly.
[06:00] Marcus: release gate call scheduled 2026-04-18 09:00PT, we'll review bisect results and QA. If threshold exceeded we roll back v2.3.
[06:15] Audience: (murmurs)
[06:22] Diego: starting bisect now, I'm cloning canary and will flip kernel commits sequentially. I'll post updates in #release-2-3.
[06:36] Linh: eval harness will produce side-by-side diffs and highlight token-level mismatch ranges; will attach graphs.
[06:50] Zoe: QA cron will run 3 cycles after bisect variants are up, and we will verify golden set passes.
[07:05] Priya: ok let's recap: owners committed, deadlines set. Marcus will prep rollback playbook and customer list. Samir will add routing split. Diego and Linh run bisect and eval. Zoe runs QA smoke. Priya drafts comms.
[07:28] Marcus: also check observability — add a custom alert for instruction-hallucination metric so we catch early.
[07:40] Priya: good, any blockers?
[07:45] Diego: nothing immediate. We'll surface if it slows.
[07:50] Linh: one ask — can we get extra GPU capacity on canary for parallel runs? It will speed bisect.
[07:58] Samir: i can allocate 2 extra slots for 12 hours, ok.
[08:06] Priya: perfect. Last thing — write meeting note and share to #product-ops. We'll reconvene in the release gate call 4/18. Thanks all.
